q: Identify which of the following statements about an information processing system is correct.
opts: Rules and information are processed to suggest decisions
Information is input and processed to produce data
Data are input and processed to produce information
Rules and information are used to produce data
why: Data provide the raw material from which information is produced. The flow is always DATA → PROCESSING → INFORMATION. Why the others are wrong: A .Rules + info produce decisions:This describes an EXPERT SYSTEM specifically.B .Information is input:This reverses the correct flow data is the input, not information.D.Rules + info produce data:This is a corruption of option A ,neither is correct for a general information processing system.

q: The finance function of Almerica Ltd uses check digits and control totals in its financial reporting system. These two input controls are a form of:
why: Check digits and control totals are methods used to ensure data entered is not incomplete or unreasonable this is the definition of data validation. Why the others are wrong: A.Data verification:Verification involves ensuring data entered matches source documents a different concept.C.Range check:A range check is simply one TYPE of data validation not the category that covers both check digits and control totals.D.Limit check:A limit check is another type of data validation, not the broader category.

q: Which type of system aims to increase the productivity of data and information workers?
why: An OAS specifically aims to increase the productivity of data and information workers. Why the others are wrong: A.Expert system:Captures human expertise for decision support not focused on worker productivity.B.Executive support system:Provides strategic information to senior managers not aimed at worker productivity.C.Decision support system:Combines data and analytical models for semi-structured decisions not productivity of data workers.

q: The use of range checks should help to deliver:
why: A range check can give some assurance that a value is accurate (e.g., months in a date should be 1–12). It gives NO assurance that all transactions have been accounted for (completeness). Why the others are wrong: A.Completeness only:Range checks CANNOT detect missing transactions at all.C.Both accuracy and completeness:Range checks cannot address completeness ,only control totals can deliver both.D.Neither:Range checks DO deliver accuracy assurance.

q: The use of control totals should help to deliver:
why: A pre-established control total will fail to reconcile if data is entered inaccurately (accuracy) OR if not all data is entered (completeness). Why the others are wrong: A.Accuracy only:Control totals also deliver completeness ,if items are missing, the total will not reconcile.B.Completeness only:Control totals also deliver accuracy incorrect entries will also cause the total to fail.D.Neither:Control totals are specifically designed to deliver both accuracy and completeness.

q: Ranger Ltd's concern that data be the same as their sources and not accidentally or deliberately altered is:
why: Integrity means data is the same as in its sources and has not been accidentally or deliberately altered. This precisely matches the scenario described. Why the others are wrong: A.Data accuracy:Accuracy means data is correct integrity has a broader meaning covering whether it has been altered.C.Data authenticity:Authenticity means data comes from bona fide sources not that it has not been altered after receipt.D.Data completeness:Completeness means all transactions are captured not the same as whether data has been altered.

q: Zing Ltd's information system automatically maintains a log of user activity. Which control objective does this system NOT effectively address?
why: The log helps PREVENT (privileges defined by log-in), DETECT (any transaction can be traced) and DETER (misuse leads to disciplinary action). The log itself cannot undo or correct what a user has already entered. Why the others are wrong: A.Prevention:The log's log-in privilege system prevents unauthorised users from accessing the system.B.Detection:Because any transaction can be traced back to a user, the log aids detection.C.Deterrence:Knowing that all activity is logged deters misuse.

q: Which statement concerning MIS and TPS is correct?
opts: An MIS is likely to be the foundation of a TPS.
MIS and TPS are usually independent.
A TPS is likely to be the foundation of an MIS.
why: The MIS concentrates on producing useful reports from internal data. Much of that data arises from transactions recorded by the TPS the TPS is the data source for the MIS. Why the others are wrong: A.MIS is foundation of TPS:This reverses the correct relationship.B.MIS and TPS are independent:They are closely linked TPS data feeds into the MIS.C.MIS and TPS are synonymous:They are different systems with different purposes.

q: Roi is the Information Systems Manager of Ajar Ltd. He is constructing a system for use by the company which includes both a 'knowledge base' and an 'inference engine'. What is Roi constructing?
why: A knowledge base (containing rules) and an inference engine (applying those rules) are the two defining components of an expert system. Why the others are wrong: A.Transaction processing system:A TPS performs and records routine transactions it has no knowledge base or inference engine.B.Management information system:An MIS produces summary reports from TPS data no knowledge base or inference engine.D.Relational database:A database stores and retrieves data it does not contain decision-making rules or an inference engine.

q: Which of the following is NOT a technical control for managing cyber risks?
why: The five technical controls are: access control, boundary firewalls and internet gateways, malware protection, patch management, and secure configuration. Risk monitoring is a management activity, not a technical control. Why the others are wrong: A.Access control:This IS one of the five technical controls.C.Patch management:This IS one of the five technical controls.D.Secure configuration:This IS one of the five technical controls.

q: A hospital has a very good record of treating and discharging its patients quickly, but it is very dependent upon its IT systems to make sure that this record is maintained. In recent years there have not been any IT system breakdowns that have adversely affected patient care. The hospital has compiled a risk map and identified the risk of a breakdown in its IT systems as being of high impact, but low probability. Identify an appropriate response to this risk by the hospital.
opts: Outsource its IT function (with a Service Level Agreement)
Accept the risk and continue to function as normal
why: For high impact, low probability risks, the appropriate response is to TRANSFER/REDUCE the risk outsourcing with an SLA achieves this. The provider takes on the risk of IT failure. Why the others are wrong: B.Close affected departments:This is avoidance appropriate for high impact AND high probability risks.C.Keep under review:Appropriate for low severity and low frequency risks.D.Accept and continue:Acceptance is appropriate for low severity risks not high impact risks.

q: The market research department of Tetro Ltd increasingly makes use of information from the internet to analyse its competitive environment and the market responses to new product offerings.Use of information from this source raises concerns regarding which characteristic of useful information?
why: The major problem with internet information is uncertainty about whether the source is reliable and authoritative anyone can publish online. Why the others are wrong: A.Completeness:Internet sources can be comprehensive completeness is not the primary concern.C.Cost-effectiveness:The internet is generally cost-effective for research.D.Relevance:Users can filter for relevant information relevance is not the key concern.

q: Identify which of the following statements about an information processing system is correct.
opts: Rules and information are processed to suggest decisions
Information is input and processed to produce data
Data are input and processed to produce information
Rules and information are used to produce data
why: Data provide the raw material from which information is produced. The flow is always DATA → PROCESSING → INFORMATION. Why the others are wrong: A .Rules + info produce decisions:This describes an EXPERT SYSTEM specifically.B .Information is input:This reverses the correct flow data is the input, not information.D.Rules + info produce data:This is a corruption of option A ,neither is correct for a general information processing system.

q: The area outside an information system's boundary is known as the:
why: Anything outside the system boundary belongs to the system's environment. The system accepts inputs from the environment and provides outputs into it. Why the others are wrong: A/B/C :Location / Setting / Context:None of these are the technical term used for the area outside the system boundary.

q: The information systems manager of Detroit Ltd wants all data input into the company's databases to be complete and accurate. As part of his information management role, he makes use of range checks.Are the following statements correct?(1) Range checks help deliver both completeness and accuracy.(2) Range checks help deliver neither completeness nor accuracy.
why: Statement 1 is false: range checks deliver accuracy only, not completeness. Statement 2 is also false: range checks DO help deliver accuracy. Why the others are wrong: A :Statement 1 only: Statement 1 is false (range checks do NOT deliver completeness).B.Statement 2 only:Statement 2 is also false (range checks DO deliver accuracy).C.Both true:Neither statement is correct.

q: The manager of Hats Ltd's information systems wants all data input into the company's databases to be accurate and complete. As part of her information management role, she makes use of control totals.Are the following statements correct?(1) Control totals help deliver both completeness and accuracy.(2) Control totals relate to data output.
why: Statement 1 is true: control totals help deliver both accuracy and completeness. Statement 2 is false: control totals relate to DATA INPUT/PROCESSING, not output. Why the others are wrong: B.Statement 2 only:Statement 1 is true control totals deliver both accuracy and completeness.C Both true: Statement 2 is false control totals relate to input, not output.D Both false: Statement 1 is true.

q: Which of the following is a characteristic of strategic information?
why: Strategic planning involves the long-term future and thus relies on estimates about future costs, revenues and conditions. Why the others are wrong: B Often very detailed: This is a characteristic of OPERATIONAL information, not strategic.C Mostly very accurate: Strategic information relies on estimates it is NOT mostly accurate.D Usually routine: Routine information is OPERATIONAL in nature.

q: Are the following statements correct?(1) Small companies have no need for internal control.(2) Small companies can use unsophisticated compensating methods.
why: All companies, including small ones, need internal controls. Statement 2 is true: small companies use less sophisticated compensating methods (e.g., greater management intervention, limited segregation). Why the others are wrong: A Statement 1 only: Statement 1 is FALSE all companies need controls.C Both true: Statement 1 is false.D Both false: Statement 2 is true.

q: Are monthly bank reconciliations and supplier statement reconciliations primarily detective controls?
why: Both monthly bank reconciliations and supplier statement reconciliations are DETECTIVE controls they take place AFTER the transactions have occurred. Why the others are wrong: A Statement 1 only: Statement 2 is also true supplier reconciliations are also detective.B Statement 2 only: Statement 1 is also true bank reconciliations are also detective.D Both false: Both are established detective controls.

q: Are the following statements correct?(1) Protection of personal data is enhanced by AI.(2) There are no ethical risks associated with AI because the human element is removed.
why: Statement 1 is false: AI can TEMPT companies to breach data protection by keeping data longer than necessary. Statement 2 is false: ethical risks (confidentiality, responsibility) still exist even when the human element is reduced. Why the others are wrong: A Statement 1 only: Statement 1 is false AI can compromise, not enhance, data protection.B Statement 2 only: Statement 2 is also false ethical risks remain.C Both true: Neither statement is correct.

q: Which of the following is NOT a likely role of the audit committee?
opts: To review the working papers of the external audit firm
To monitor the independence of the external auditor
To monitor the effectiveness of internal audit
To make recommendations regarding the external auditor
why: The audit committee acts in an overseeing capacity. The external auditor's working papers are the property of the external audit firm the committee does not review them. Why the others are wrong: B Monitor independence of external auditor: This IS a legitimate role of the audit committee.C Monitor effectiveness of internal audit: This IS a legitimate role of the audit committee.D Make recommendations re external auditor: This IS a legitimate role of the audit committee.

q: Are the following statements correct?(1) Authorised storeroom access is a physical control.(2) Agreeing signed despatch records to sales orders is an information processing control.
why: Statement 1 is true: authorised storeroom access is a physical control. Statement 2 is true: agreeing signed despatch records to sales orders is an information processing control (application-specific reconciliation). Why the others are wrong: A or B Only one true: Both statements are independently correct.D Both false: Both are well-established examples of their respective control types.

q: Controls in an IT system are classified as general IT controls or information processing controls.Are the following statements correct?(1) Staff training is classified as an information processing control.(2) Password protection is classified as an information processing control.
why: Staff training and password protection are GENERAL IT controls they affect all applications across the entire IT environment, not specific individual application processes. Why the others are wrong: A Statement 1 only: Staff training is a GENERAL IT control Statement 1 is false.B Statement 2 only: Password protection is a GENERAL IT control Statement 2 is also false.C Both true: Neither training nor passwords are information processing controls.

q: Controls in an IT system are classified as general IT controls or information processing controls.Are the following statements correct?(1) Password protection is a general IT control.(2) One-for-one checking is an information processing control.
why: Password protection IS a general IT control (affects all applications). One-for-one checking IS an information processing control (checks a specific application's output against source documents). Why the others are wrong: A Statement 1 only: Statement 2 is also correct one-for-one checking is application-specific.B Statement 2 only: Statement 1 is also correct passwords are general IT controls.D Both false: Both statements are correct.

q: Controls in an IT system are classified as general IT controls or information processing controls.Are the following statements correct?(1) Cyclical review of master files is a general IT control.(2) Back-up power sources are general IT controls.
why: Statement 1 is FALSE: cyclical review of master files is an INFORMATION PROCESSING control (specific to one application). Statement 2 is TRUE: back-up power sources support the entire IT environment a general IT control. Why the others are wrong: A Statement 1 only: Statement 1 is false master file reviews are IP controls.C Both true: Statement 1 is false.D Both false: Statement 2 is true.

q: Controls in an IT system are classified as general IT controls or information processing controls.Are the following statements correct?(1) Back-up power sources are general IT controls.(2) Computer maintenance agreements and insurance are general IT controls.
why: Both back-up power sources AND computer maintenance agreements/insurance are general IT controls they affect the operation of all applications across the entire IT environment. Why the others are wrong: A or B Only one true: Both are independently correct general IT controls.D Both false: Both are established examples of general IT controls.

q: Which of the following is NOT a component of a system of internal controls?
why: Strategy-devising is a function of the board of directors. The five components of internal control are: Control Environment, Risk Assessment Process, Information System & Communication, Control Activities, and Monitoring. Why the others are wrong: A Control environment: IS one of the five components of internal control.C Risk assessment process: IS one of the five components of internal control.D Control activities: IS one of the five components of internal control.

q: The following statements refer to possible limitations of a system of internal control.Are the following statements correct?(1) Controls are ineffective if staff collude in fraud.(2) Controls are designed for both routine and non-routine transactions.
why: Statement 1 is TRUE: collusion (people working together to defraud) renders controls ineffective. Statement 2 is FALSE: controls are largely designed for ROUTINE transactions, not both routine and non-routine. Why the others are wrong: B Statement 2 only: Statement 2 is false controls are mainly for routine transactions.C Both true: Statement 2 is false.D Both false: Statement 1 is true collusion is a recognised limitation.

q: The following statements refer to possible limitations of a system of internal control. For each statement, select whether it is true or false.Are the following statements correct?(1) Controls deal mainly with non-routine transactions.(2) Senior management can never ignore internal controls.
why: Statement 1 is FALSE: controls deal mainly with ROUTINE transactions (not non-routine). Statement 2 is also FALSE: senior management MAY be able to ignore internal controls this is a recognised inherent limitation. Why the others are wrong: A Statement 1 only: Statement 1 is false controls are for routine situations.B Statement 2 only: Statement 2 is also false senior management CAN ignore controls.C Both true: Both statements are false.

q: Why is segregation of duties important?
opts: It helps to immediately detect all errors.
It eliminates the need for other controls.
It ensures errors can never occur.
why: Segregation of duties ensures that fraud and misstatement are prevented or detected specifically, no single person can complete an entire fraudulent transaction without another person's involvement. Why the others are wrong: A Immediately detect all errors: Segregation does not guarantee immediate detection of every error.C Eliminates need for other controls: Other controls are still needed alongside segregation of duties.D Ensures errors can never occur: Errors can still occur segregation of duties reduces, not eliminates, the risk.

q: Are these statements correct?(1) Information systems comprise only IT.(2) They include the process of preparing financial statements.
why: Statement 1 is FALSE: information systems comprise ALL information flows (hardcopy and electronic) not only IT. Statement 2 is TRUE: IS includes the process of preparing financial statements. Why the others are wrong: A Statement 1 only: Statement 1 is false IS is broader than just IT.C Both true: Statement 1 is false.D Both false: Statement 2 is true.

q: Are the following statements correct?(1) Off-site program storage is a general IT control.(2) Input field check programs are general IT controls.
why: Statement 1 is TRUE: off-site program storage is a general IT control (protects all programs across the entire environment). Statement 2 is FALSE: input field check programs are INFORMATION PROCESSING controls (specific to individual applications). Why the others are wrong: B Statement 2 only: Statement 2 is false input field checks are IP controls.C Both true: Statement 2 is false.D Both false: Statement 1 is true.

q: Controls in an IT system are classified as general IT controls or information processing controlAre the following statements correct?(1) Input field check programs are information processing controls.(2) Manual checks for input authorisation are information processing controls.
why: Input field check programs ARE information processing controls (specific to applications). Manual checks for input authorisation ARE also information processing controls they directly address the validity of transactions in specific applications. Why the others are wrong: A or B Only one true: Both are independently information processing controls.D Both false: Both are established examples of IP controls.

q: Most entities make use of IT systems for financial reporting and operational purposes. Controls operating in an IT environment can be split into general IT controls and information processing controls.Which of the following represents an information processing control?
opts: Storing extra copies of programs off-site
Cyclical reviews of all master files
why: Cyclical reviews of master files relate to a specific application's data they are information processing controls. The other options (virus protection, backup power, off-site storage) are general IT controls. Why the others are wrong: A Virus protection: This is a GENERAL IT control.B Backup power sources: This is a GENERAL IT control.C Off-site program storage: This is a GENERAL IT control.

q: Which of the following represents an inherent limitation of a system of internal control?
opts: The possibility that staff members will collude in fraud
why: Staff collusion is an INHERENT limitation it cannot be designed away entirely even with a well-functioning system of controls. The other options describe control deficiencies, not inherent limitations. Why the others are wrong: A Management override: While a limitation, it is more of a deficiency than an inherent limitation.B Poorly trained staff: This is a control deficiency that can be remedied.C Inadequate documentation: This is a control deficiency that can be remedied.

q: Which of the following is NOT a general IT control?
opts: Procedures for resubmission of rejected data
why: Resubmission procedures relate to handling rejected input data within a SPECIFIC application this is an information processing control, not a general IT control. Why the others are wrong: A Passwords: Passwords ARE a general IT control they apply to the entire environment.B Backup power sources: Backup power IS a general IT control supports all applications.D Program libraries: Program libraries ARE general IT controls manage all programs.
